items.title: The injectivity situation reduces to localizations of polynomial algebras with finitely presented modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if the asserted conclusion holds for every Situation labelled situation-mod-injective with a fixed local ring A_0, with B a localization of a polynomial algebra over A_0 and N of finite presentation over B, then it holds for every such situation with A = A_0 (statement lines 7044-7051). The proof takes an arbitrary A -> B with u : N -> M and writes B = C/I with C the localization of a polynomial algebra over A at a prime, observing that showing N finitely presented as a C-module suffices by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-finitely-presented-over-subring, so one may assume B is such a localization (proof lines 7053-7060). Writing N = B^{oplus n}/K, the proof uses that B/m_A B is Noetherian, being essentially of finite type over a field, to choose finitely many elements k_1, ..., k_s of K such that the submodule K' they generate satisfies N'/m_A N' = N/m_A N for N' = B^{oplus n}/K' (proof lines 7062-7066). If the conclusion holds for the composition u' : N' -> M then u' is injective, hence N' = N and u' = u, so the conclusion transfers to the original situation (proof lines 7068-7070). Approximating the presentation of N modulo the maximal ideal so that the smaller module can be substituted is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
